title: Telemetry intake transformer and dual-sink orchestrator
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight intake transformer that normalizes inbound telemetry (structured logs, plain text logs, and event payloads), attaches or validates correlation IDs, and forwards to both Loki and Elasticsearch-compatible sinks. This task implements a dual-sink orchestrator inside the ingest plane so we can operate Loki for high-cardinality traces and ES for long-term analytic queries, without forcing producers to emit separate formats. Key constraints: keep per-request latency added by the transformer <6ms p95, avoid synchronous downstream enrichments that increase tail latency, and provide schema negotiation to support mixed legacy producers.
acceptance_criteria: Transformer accepts JSON, NDJSON, and plain-text logs and emits a canonical JSON envelope with fields: timestamp, level, message, trace_id, span_id, tenant_id, service, metadata
Missing trace_id/span_id are generated deterministically when absent and stamped with provenance header (x-ingest-generated=true)
Dual-sink orchestrator writes to Loki (labels+line) and ES-ingest topic with the canonical envelope using the existing ingestion protocol
End-to-end roundtrip added latency from proxy to both sinks is <6ms p95 under normal load (single small event path) and <25ms p95 under high throughput with batching enabled
Configurable sampling for high-volume tenants (per-tenant sampler TTL) is available and respected upstream before ES fanout
Unit and integration tests cover schema negotiation, missing-correlation-id generation, and backpressure scenarios
Runbook updated and a Gated rollout plan exists with canary traffic routing and monitoring dashboards
implementation_notes: Place transformer as a stateless layer in the ingest-proxy (Envoy Lua or Rust filter) to avoid an extra hop
Use a small in-memory LRU cache for tenant->tenant_id mapping to avoid remote lookups for the hot path
Asynchronous enrichment (e.g., lookup of heavy metadata) will be implemented as background worker that emits follow-up enrichment events rather than blocking the intake path
Dual-sink fanout implemented via durable write to Kafka topic 'ingest.canonical.v1' then separate connectors: Loki-forwarder and ES-forwarder consume from it
To meet latency SLOs, keep transformer CPU allocations modest and add token-bucket rate limiting per-tenant to protect downstream sinks
Schema negotiation: support v1 (flat) and v2 (structured) manifests; unknown fields are preserved under metadata. Producers can opt-in to strict mode which rejects incompatible schemas
Dedup window: use event fingerprinting (hash of tenant_id+trace_id+timestamp bucket) in forwarder to prevent duplicate writes during retries
testing_plan: Load tests in staging with synthetic multi-tenant traffic: 10k rps mixed sizes to measure p95 latency to both sinks
Fault injection: drop Loki sink, ensure ES-forwarder continues, verify replay from Kafka recovers lost writes
Property tests for correlation-id propagation and deterministic generation
E2E smoke test that validates a trace across HTTP request -> transformer -> Loki labels -> Console trace link
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal telemetry only (10% of traffic) with strict logging and verbose tracing
Phase 2: selected customer tenants (opt-in) with sampling enabled for noisy tenants
Phase 3: global rollout with rate-limit guardrails and automated rollback on error spikes
Monitoring: add per-tenant telemetry_injector error rate, transformer latency, and sink-lag dashboards
